essays.question: What excites you about Acme?
essays.answer:
Acme is turning software creation into something people do in natural language, and I have seen what that does inside a business. At AdFixus I taught a commercial team to vibe-code against a central AI brain, so sellers built their own enablement tools instead of needing an enablement team to exist. My own 14-agent operating system on n8n, Supabase, Anthropic and OpenAI started as two agents. Acme puts that kind of building in front of millions of people, and that changes who gets to build.

The corporate development seat excites me because the hard calls at a company like this are build, buy or partner. I made that call with a major media publisher. A day of pressure-testing landed on partner now and revisit build in twelve months, which saved roughly a year of engineering time. For Meliora I wrote the ventures thesis behind Meliora Fund One, focused on CTO-led founders and application-layer AI ventures. At Nexxen I drove cross-functional alignment through two technology M&As that took APAC platform revenue from $4m to $38m.

In the first weeks I would sit with product, AI and engineering leaders, turn their priorities into acquisition themes, and put every target through the same build, buy or partner screen, with owners and success measures set before close.

essays.question: If you want to share something you built with Acme please share below.
essays.answer: The build I would point to sits on a different stack: n8n, Supabase, Anthropic and OpenAI rather than Acme. It is a 14-agent, 45-workflow autonomous AI operating system I have run in production for the last 18 months, grown from two agents. Supabase holds agent identities, task queues and execution state. Deterministic workflows act as the rails, and a non-deterministic swarm handles outbound, editorial, competitive sweeps and guest scouting. A failure-to-system engine writes a permanent rule and drafts the fix the second time anything breaks. Internal actions run on their own; anything that leaves the building waits for a human go or no-go. I have licensed stack components to three businesses and launched three SaaS products alongside it (Ctrl, Circle, Pulse). It matters for this seat because it taught me what separates a demo from a system. Twelve days in, a platform update silently broke most of the fleet, and the auditor I built to catch that sent a 3am message saying everything was healthy, because it was broken the same way. That is the lens I would bring to assessing teams and technologies for Acme: does it hold up when you are not watching it. I can walk through the system live.

record.posting: About Acme Acme enables marketers to buy creator led ads as easily and scalably as Meta or Google ads, automating sourcing, pricing, contracting, delivery, and measurement with AI, so work that took months now happens in minutes. As these dollars move, they need performance-grade pipes; Acme is how those dollars flow to creators with the speed, control, and measurement marketers expect. We enable brands like Uber, DoorDash, and Bombas to run creator campaigns with the same rigor, control, and accountability as their core performance channels. Acme has raised $56M to date at a $340M valuation , including a recent Series B led by Forerunner , which followed our Series A within a calendar year. Our investors also include Benchmark, Craft, and AlleyCorp . Acme has been named to Forbes’ Next Billion Dollar Startups, 2025 , and our platform is already used and loved by the world’s leading marketers and creators. We are just getting started! Acme will be the infrastructure that enables hundreds of billions of paid media dollars, to shift to creators. Our business is hyperscaling, with many thousands of the best creators in the world filling demand from the world’s best brands. As Acme's first Head of Creator Growth, you'll own that motion: the product loops, referral mechanics, paid and organic channels, and activation systems that bring creators onto the platform and to get them earning fast. Mass-supply marketplace expansion to meet unparalleled demand requires dedicated ownership - and you’ll be that owner. Obsessively AI-native mindset and ways of working. Strong command of unit economics and experimentation. About You You are a marketplace savant. You're laser-focused on outcomes - activated, earning creators, not signups or vanity metrics. You are insatiably curious. Constantly reading, listening to podcasts from the best operators and investors, and obsessing over the latest model releases. record.posting: About Acme Acme is the open AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers, without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. As enterprise adoption of AI accelerates, Acme sits at the center of how organizations operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads. About the Role This role is ideal for someone who has supported early-stage GTM teams and knows how to create clarity from chaos. You should be analytical, detail-oriented, and technically strong, with the ability to partner cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, and Finance. If you want to build the operational backbone of a category-defining GTM team, this is the right fit. What You'll Do GTM Architecture & Planning Own the GTM Architecture: Define segments, coverage models, and the planning logic that turns Acme's product and growth strategy into a scalable revenue engine. Lead Annual Planning End-to-End: Drive capacity modeling, demand generation targets, account/territory design, quota allocation, and the headcount and expense plans that drive the org. Strategic Initiatives: Identify through data and process fluency what's driving KPIs (conversions, ACV, usage growth) and partner with functional leaders to advise on experiments to affect change. Incentive & Quota Design: Design comp plans that reward our north star metrics and manage the end-to-end quota methodology to keep targets equitable across a rapidly scaling business. GTM Engineering & Systems Tech Stack Strategy & Architecture: Own the roadmap and design for our GTM systems (e.g., CRM, CPQ, prospecting tools, etc). Conduct field discovery to identify high-impact workflow opportunities and own the implementation and delivery of outcomes. Agentic Automation & Process Replacement: Lead projects that systematically eliminate manual "debt." Build systems and workflows that create leverage and scale the organization faster than headcount. Multi-Channel Integration & Data Governance: Orchestrate data flow across the GTM stack ,  product usage data, billing, CRM, and support ,  ensuring reliable, high-quality single source of truth. Act as the primary liaison to Data and Product teams on behalf of the GTM organization. Operating Cadence & Governance Support the Operating Cadence: Partner with leadership on forecast roll-ups, pipeline and consumption reviews, and QBR/MBR support. Financial Controllership: Partner tightly with Finance on headcount and expense management, compensation modeling, revenue forecast accuracy, and variance analysis. Team Leadership: Hire, mentor, and develop a small, high-leverage team of analysts, systems engineers, and business partners. Design the infrastructure that lets a lean revenue operations team scale with Acme's rapid growth. What We're Looking For Experience: 10+ years in revenue operations, sales strategy, GTM finance, or systems engineering, including at least five years leading cross-functional teams ,  ideally in a usage-based, API, or infrastructure/dev-tools business. Planning Mastery: Deep fluency with capacity models, account/territory design, quota allocation, comp modeling, and forecasting. Technical & Architecture Expertise: Strong background designing and integrating GTM tech stacks. You bring a product-management mindset to process design. Full-Funnel Perspective: Experience across the full customer lifecycle ,  from demand generation and pipeline management, to PLG and SLG, and driving adoption and expansion of our customers.. Communication & Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal skills, with a track record presenting to executives and translating between functional areas and teams. record.posting: About the Role Acme is building the AI-native cloud ,  the fastest inference infrastructure on the planet, paired with a model ecosystem, orchestration layer, and data center footprint that enterprises and frontier labs depend on. As we expand the surface area through which our models and inference reach end users, we're hiring a Head of Distribution Partnerships to source and build the 0-to-1 partnerships that drive token distribution from models served on Acme. This is a builder role for someone with sharp technical instincts and a strong product-partnerships background who can identify where Acme's competitive edge in open-source model serving complements another platform's distribution ,  and then go build that relationship from scratch. You'll work across technology partnerships, co-sell motions, ISV integrations, and OEM arrangements with data platforms, cloud providers, and software ecosystems where our inference and OSS model serving capabilities create obvious joint value. You need technical fluency to scope integrations with engineering counterparts, product instincts to identify where Acme's serving stack creates a compelling wedge, and the hustle to turn a cold outreach into a signed, launched partnership. You'll report into the VP of Strategic Partnerships and work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and the broader Partnerships team. Responsibilities Source and Build 0-to-1 Partnerships: Identify and prioritize distribution partners ,  data platforms, cloud marketplaces, ISVs, and software ecosystems ,  where Acme's open-source model serving and inference performance is a differentiated fit. Build these relationships from first contact through signed agreement and launch. Structure Technical & Commercial Integrations: Design partnership structures across technology integrations, co-sell arrangements, ISV partnerships, and OEM deals. Scope technical integration requirements directly with partner engineering teams and negotiate the commercial terms alongside them. Own the Partner Lifecycle: Manage the full arc of a partnership ,  pipeline generation, technical scoping, commercial negotiation, legal review, launch, and ongoing account growth ,  with less structure and more ambiguity than a mature partner program. Translate Product Fit into Partner Value: Work closely with Product and Engineering to understand where Acme's model serving and inference capabilities offer a genuine wedge into a partner's ecosystem, and translate that into a partnership pitch that resonates with partner stakeholders. Drive Joint Go-to-Market: Partner with Marketing and Sales to build joint co-sell motions, marketplace listings, and case studies that demonstrate real distribution impact from launched partnerships. Requirements Experience: At least 5 years in product partnerships, business development, or technical alliance management, ideally at an infrastructure, developer tools, or platform company. 0-to-1 Builder Mentality: Track record of sourcing and closing partnerships from scratch ,  comfortable with ambiguity, cold outreach, and building process where none exists yet. Technical Acumen: Enough technical depth to scope integrations directly with engineering counterparts ,  APIs, SDKs, model serving, or infrastructure integrations ,  without needing a technical partner in every conversation. Commercial Structuring: Experience negotiating technology partnership agreements, co-sell frameworks, ISV/OEM arrangements, or marketplace integrations. High EQ & Self-Starter: Comfortable operating with significant autonomy, building trust with partner stakeholders quickly, and prioritizing across a broad and evolving partner landscape. Preferred Qualifications Experience partnering with or working inside data platforms, cloud marketplaces, or enterprise software ecosystems. Background in AI infrastructure, model serving, or inference, or strong familiarity with the open-source model ecosystem. Experience with marketplace private offers, co-sell motions, or consumption-based commercial models. About Acme Acme, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Acme serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. answers.question: If you want to share something you built with Acme please share below.
answers.answer: The thing I would share is the operating system I built to run my own practice, mind/make, for the past 18 months. It brings me customers, produces content and prepares my sales meetings. The second time anything breaks, it writes a permanent rule so the failure does not repeat. Anything that leaves the building waits for my go or no-go. Components of it are now licensed to three businesses. Running it on my own p&l means I reprice weekly against volatile model costs and decide what stays in-house and what gets licensed out. I bring the same discipline to clients' build, buy or partner calls. A major media publisher's CRO had refereed two quarters of build-versus-partner debate. After one day of pressure-testing the decision was to partner now and revisit build in twelve months. The agreement was signed the following month, and roughly a year of engineering time was not spent on the wrong thing. A top-10 US digital publisher had 14 AI vendors on the calendar. I wrote a three-decision board memo: one vendor killed, one workflow built internally, one paused with a re-evaluation date. I am happy to walk you through the system and those decisions in one conversation.

answers.question: What excites you about Acme?
answers.answer: Acme lets anyone with an idea ship software, and that shift is moving faster than any single team can build. That makes buy and partner as important as build, and I want to own those calls. My career has sat where a new technology meets a P&L. At Nexxen (Singtel) we scaled APAC platform revenue from $4m to $38m across 12 fragmented markets through two technology M&As. The hard part came after close: aligning product, engineering, sales and operations so the acquired capability became revenue. More recently I ran a day of pressure-testing for a major media publisher's CRO on a build-versus-partner split. We chose partner now and revisit build in twelve months; the agreement signed the following month and roughly a year of engineering time was not spent on the wrong thing. For a top-10 US publisher with 14 AI vendors on the calendar, I wrote a three-decision board memo: one vendor killed, one workflow built internally, one paused with a re-evaluation date. I also co-launched Meliora Fund One, with a thesis on CTO-led founders and application-layer AI ventures, which puts me in the founder and investor conversations where targets surface early. I want to be the first corporate development hire, build the pipeline and own each deal through to integration.
